title: Sex Determination, Sex Expression and Stability in Breeding

content.overview: Cannabis sex determination has a strong chromosomal genetic basis, while observed floral sex expression is also influenced by development, hormones, genotype and environment. Breeding records should therefore distinguish genetic sex evidence, induced expression and spontaneous instability.

vocabulary.definition: A population or species condition in which male and female flowers are normally borne on separate individuals.
The floral sexual phenotype actually expressed by a plant at a given time and condition.
Induction or expression of male flowers on genetically female material; feminized-seed programs may use controlled sex reversal but require validated methods and progeny verification.

sections.title: Genetic sex and floral expression are related but not identical observations
sections.body: Chromosomal sex systems contribute strongly to cannabis sex determination, while hormone signaling, development and environmental conditions can influence expression.

sections.title: Instability should be recorded as a phenotype
sections.body: Spontaneous opposite-sex floral expression should be documented by genotype, timing, location and environmental context. Current evidence does not justify assuming one universal trigger or confirmed predisposition for every cultivar.

sections.title: Feminized seed quality still requires progeny evidence
sections.body: Controlled sex reversal can produce pollen from XX plants for feminized-seed production, but stock selection, process control and progeny verification remain important; a label alone is not a biological guarantee.

workedExamples: A plant expressing one late male flower after severe stress should be recorded separately from a line repeatedly expressing intersex flowers across normal replicated conditions.
A feminized seed lot should be evaluated through progeny observations rather than assumed perfect from production method alone.
commonMistakes: Equating any environmental stress with guaranteed hermaphroditism.
Treating feminized as synonymous with zero sex-expression risk.
Failing to distinguish intentionally induced sex reversal from spontaneous instability.
content.practicalApplication: Use a sex-expression log recording plant ID, genetic-sex evidence if available, floral phenotype, developmental stage, environmental context, whether expression was intentionally induced, and progeny outcomes.
content.summary: Advanced breeding separates sex determination from observed sex expression and evaluates stability through documented, replicated evidence.
